Piotrkow Trybunalski Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Piotrków Trybunalski, Poland

Demolished. Piotrków, a royal city under Magdeburg Law after 1292, barred Jewish residence within its walls from at least the 16th century; a 1657 pogrom during the 'Swedish Deluge' killed about 50 Jewish families and expelled the rest. King Jan III Sobieski's 1679 privilege permitted Jewish return and formal community establishment, including this original cemetery beside a new synagogue complex in Podzamcze - previously, Piotrków's Jews had been buried in nearby Rozprza's community cemetery. The town later became a residence for various tzadikim and, from 1864, a major Hebrew printing center; by 1929, roughly 11,000 (28%) of 49,000 residents were Jewish. This cemetery functioned until 1795, when 19th-century city-border adjustments repurposed most of its edges for a new street (today's Wojska Polskiego Street) and hospital buildings; German forces completely devastated the remaining site during WWII.
